name: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS Predator HX-9 Combat Eye
description:
The Predator HX-9 is a full ocular replacement engineered for frontline combat operators, housing a multi-spectrum sensor array behind ballistic-grade synthetic cornea. The unit integrates real-time IFF tagging, trajectory prediction overlays, and threat-priority ranking via a dedicated co-processor wired directly to the optic nerve. Micro-gyroscopic stabilization compensates for motion blur during high-speed engagements, and a hardened EMP-resistant shell protects core functions in electronic warfare environments.

Distribution is restricted to licensed military contractors, CorpSec units, and credentialed mercenary outfits — civilian acquisition requires black-market sourcing at significant legal risk. On the streets of Meridian's lower tiers, a salvaged pair of HX-9s is considered a trophy, and runners who sport them are either genuinely dangerous or desperately want to seem so.
installation_requirements: Certified combat-cybernetics surgeon; neural interface compatibility assessment; optic nerve sheathing recommended
rejection_risk: Moderate — synthetic cornea and co-processor integration stresses optic nerve; elevated risk without pre-installation nerve sheathing
maintenance: Quarterly firmware sync with ARCTURUS servers; lens recalibration every 6 months; co-processor coolant flush annually

side_effects: Persistent threat-tagging of civilians in crowded environments causes anxiety and hypervigilance
Co-processor heat buildup during sustained engagement causes mild periorbital discomfort
IFF overlays can bleed into REM sleep, producing vivid combat-scenario dreams
Incompatibility with consumer AR platforms — civilian HUD software causes system conflicts
cultural_context: HX-9s are the eye of choice for Meridian's private military ecosystem, and their distinctive matte-black sclera and faint reticle glow are immediately recognizable to anyone who operates in that world. Possessing a pair without military credentials is a serious offense under the Great Lakes Augmentation Control Act, but enforcement is inconsistent in Shelf and Rack districts. CorpSec operators who go freelance often keep their HX-9s, making them walking legal violations — and everyone knows it.
known_users: Organized crime enforcers with deep pockets
story_hooks: A murdered CorpSec lieutenant is found with both HX-9s surgically removed post-mortem — someone needed the IFF database still loaded in the co-processor
A runner's salvaged HX-9 pair keeps tagging a specific civilian in the crowd as a high-priority hostile — and the system won't say why
ARCTURUS sends a retrieval team to recover a pair of HX-9s from a Shelf-district fixer, claiming the units contain classified target data from an ongoing operation
